questions.q: What went wrong with the first draft Copilot generated in this lesson's worked example?
options: It ran successfully but silently dropped the request to exclude cancelled orders, producing a real but wrong number
It threw a syntax error and never executed
It correctly implemented every part of the prompt
It failed to read the sales.csv file at all
questions.explain: The prompt asked to exclude cancelled orders; the generated groupBy/sum never filtered them out, even though the code ran cleanly.

questions.q: Why is it dangerous that the flawed first draft 'ran without error'?
options: Because running successfully and producing a plausible number can mask that part of the actual request was silently dropped
Because code that runs without error is always correct
Because Spark never produces output unless the logic is correct
It isn't dangerous — running without error is sufficient proof of correctness
questions.explain: Plausible and running successfully isn't the same as correct — that's exactly why review has to be a habit, not a formality.

questions.q: According to the review checklist in this lesson, what should you check before accepting a generated cell?
options: Whether every clause in your prompt actually shows up in the code, and whether the numbers hold up on a small sample
Only whether the code executes without throwing an exception
Only whether the code is syntactically valid Python
Whether the code was generated faster than you could type it yourself
questions.explain: The checklist: match every prompt clause, check real schema column names, check null handling, and run on a sample to verify actual numbers.

questions.q: What was the fix for the missing filter in the corrected version of the notebook cell?
options: Add a filter for order_status != 'CANCELLED' before grouping and aliasing the aggregated column
Rewrite the entire notebook from scratch in a different language
Remove the groupBy clause entirely
Switch from PySpark to KQL to avoid the issue
questions.explain: The corrected code filters out cancelled orders with col("order_status") != "CANCELLED" before grouping by region and summing revenue.

questions.q: How does this lesson's review habit connect to later material in the chapter?
options: It's the same practice Lesson 58, 'Evaluating AI Output for Correctness,' turns into a repeatable habit across tests, documentation, and anomaly checks
It has no connection to any other lesson in this chapter
It only applies to PySpark and never generalizes to other generated output
It replaces the need for Lesson 58 entirely
questions.explain: This worked example is the concrete case; Lesson 58 generalizes the same review discipline across the rest of the pipeline.
